# Load in Data

```{r}
train <- read.csv('Data/train.csv')
```

# Data Processing

## Data Cleaning

Let's take a look at which variables have NA values

```{r}
sapply(names(train), function(col_name) {
  sum(is.na(train[col_name]))
})
```

```{r}
train_clean <- train

# Id
## Remove Id
train_clean$Id <- NULL 

# Lot Frontage
## NAs likely just houses with no street access
train_clean$LotFrontage[is.na(train_clean$LotFrontage)] <- 0 

# Alley
## NAs just houses with no alley access
train_clean$Alley[is.na(train_clean$Alley)] <- 'NoAlley' 

# MasVnrType & MasVnrArea
## Only 8 NAs, best to remove
train_clean <- train_clean[!is.na(train_clean$MasVnrType),] 
train_clean <- train_clean[!is.na(train_clean$MasVnrArea),] 

# BsmtQual, BsmtCond, BsmtExposure, BsmtFinType1, BsmtFinType2
## NAs are houses without basements
train_clean$BsmtQual[is.na(train_clean$BsmtQual) == TRUE] <- 'NoBsmt'
train_clean$BsmtCond[is.na(train_clean$BsmtCond) == TRUE] <- 'NoBsmt'
train_clean$BsmtExposure[is.na(train_clean$BsmtExposure) == TRUE] <- 'NoBsmt'
train_clean$BsmtFinType1[is.na(train_clean$BsmtFinType1) == TRUE] <- 'NoBsmt'
train_clean$BsmtFinType2[is.na(train_clean$BsmtFinType2) == TRUE] <- 'NoBsmt'

# Electrical
## Only 1 NA, best to remove
train_clean <- train_clean[!is.na(train_clean$Electrical),] 

# FireplaceQu
## NAs from houses not having fireplaces
train_clean[train_clean$Fireplaces == 0, 'FireplaceQu'] <- 'NoFrplc' 

# GarageType, GarageFinish, GarageQual, GarageCond
## NAs from houses not having garages
train_clean$GarageType[is.na(train_clean$GarageType) == TRUE] <- 'NoGarage'
train_clean$GarageFinish[is.na(train_clean$GarageFinish) == TRUE] <- 'NoGarage'
train_clean$GarageQual[is.na(train_clean$GarageQual) == TRUE] <- 'NoGarage'
train_clean$GarageCond[is.na(train_clean$GarageCond) == TRUE] <- 'NoGarage'

# GarageYrBuilt
## All NAs also when GarageArea == 0, just houses with no garage
train_clean$GarageYrBlt[is.na(train_clean$GarageYrBlt) == TRUE] <- 0

# PoolQC
## All NAs when PoolArea == 0
train_clean[train_clean$PoolArea == 0, 'PoolQC'] <- 'NoPool' 

# Frence
## NAs are houses with no fence
train_clean$Fence[is.na(train_clean$Fence)] <- 'NoFence' 

# MiscFeature
## NAs are houses with no misc feature
train_clean$MiscFeature[is.na(train_clean$MiscFeature)] <- 'NoMisc' 

sapply(names(train_clean), function(col_name) {
  sum(is.na(train_clean[col_name]))
})
```

## Data Formatting

Let's factor the categorical data

```{r}
cat_vars <- c('MSSubClass', 'MSZoning', 'Street', 'Alley', 'LotShape', 'LandContour', 'Utilities', 'LotConfig', 'LandSlope', 'Neighborhood', 'Condition1', 'Condition2', 'BldgType', 'HouseStyle', 'RoofStyle', 'RoofMatl', 'Exterior1st', 'Exterior2nd', 'MasVnrType', 'ExterQual', 'ExterCond', 'Foundation', 'BsmtQual', 'BsmtCond', 'BsmtExposure', 'BsmtFinType1', 'BsmtFinType2', 'Heating', 'HeatingQC', 'CentralAir', 'Electrical', 'KitchenQual', 'Functional', 'FireplaceQu', 'GarageType', 'GarageFinish', 'GarageQual', 'GarageCond', 'PavedDrive', 'PoolQC', 'Fence', 'MiscFeature', 'MoSold', 'SaleType', 'SaleCondition')

train_form <- train_clean %>%
  dplyr::mutate(across(all_of(cat_vars), factor))
```

### Sparse Categorical Levels

#### MSSubClass

```{r}
table(train_form$MSSubClass)
ggplot(train_form, aes(x = MSSubClass, y = SalePrice)) + 
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = 'SalePrice by MSSubClass')
```

```{r}
# 20 and 40 are similar categories (both 1-story) and are similar in their SalePrice distributions
train_form <- dplyr::mutate(
  train_form, 
  MSSubClass = ifelse(MSSubClass == '40', '20', as.character(MSSubClass)),
  MSSubClass = factor(MSSubClass)
)
table(train_form$MSSubClass)
```

#### Condition1 and Condition2

```{r}
table(train_form$Condition1)

  labs(title = 'SalePrice by Condition1')

table(train_form$Condition2)
ggplot(train_form, aes(x = Condition2, y = SalePrice)) + 
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = 'SalePrice by Condition2')
```

```{r}
# Conditon1 & 2 have the same levels.  Manual conversion to separate dummy variables with Norm as baseline
# Merge PosN and PosA into 'POS', near or adjacent to positive off-site feature
# Merge RRNn and RRAn, RRNe and RRAe, into RRn (adjacent or near North-South rail) and RRe (adjacent or near East-West rail)
train_form <- dplyr::mutate(
  train_form,
  CondArt = case_when(
    Condition1 == 'Artery' | Condition2 == 'Artery' ~ 1,
    TRUE ~ 0
  ),
  CondFdr = case_when(
    Condition1 == 'Feedr' | Condition2 == 'Feedr' ~ 1,
    TRUE ~ 0
  ),
  CondPos = case_when(
    Condition1 %in% c('PosN', 'PosA') | Condition2 %in% c('PosN', 'PosA') ~ 1,
    TRUE ~ 0
  ),
  CondRRn = case_when(
    Condition1 %in% c('RRNn', 'RRAn') | Condition2 %in% c('RRNn', 'RRAn') ~ 1,
    TRUE ~ 0
  ),
  CondRRe = case_when(
    Condition1 %in% c('RRNe', 'RRAe') | Condition2 %in% c('RRNe', 'RRAe') ~ 1,
    TRUE ~ 0
  )
)

head(train_form[c('Condition1', 'Condition2', 'CondArt', 'CondFdr', 'CondPos', 'CondRRn', 'CondRRe')])
```

```{r}
# Remove Condition1 & 2
train_form$Condition1 <- NULL
train_form$Condition2 <- NULL
```

#### Exterior1st and Exterior2nd

```{r}
table(train_form$Exterior1st)
ggplot(train_form, aes(x = Exterior1st, y = SalePrice)) + 
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = 'SalePrice by Exterior1st') +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 270))

table(train_form$Exterior2nd)
ggplot(train_form, aes(x = Exterior2nd, y = SalePrice)) + 
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = 'SalePrice by Exterior2nd') +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 270))
```

```{r}
# Exterior1st & 2nd have the same levels.  Manual conversion to separate categorical variables with "no" response as base for each
# Merge AsphShn, CBlock, Stone into Other
# Merge BrkComm, BrkCmn, Brk Cmn into Brick
train_form <- dplyr::mutate(
  train_form,
  ExtAsb = ifelse(Exterior1st == 'AsbShng' | Exterior2nd == 'AsbShng', 1, 0),
  ExtBrk = case_when(
    Exterior1st %in% c('BrkComm', 'Brk Cmn', 'BrkFace') ~ 1,
    Exterior2nd %in% c('BrkComm', 'Brk Cmn', 'BrkFace') ~ 1,
    TRUE ~ 0
  ),
  ExtCem = case_when(
    Exterior1st %in% c('CemntBd', 'CmentBd') ~ 1,
    Exterior2nd %in% c('CemntBd', 'CmentBd') ~ 1,
    TRUE ~ 0
  ),
  ExtHdB = ifelse(Exterior1st == 'HdBoard' | Exterior2nd == 'HdBoard', 1, 0),
  ExtImS = ifelse(Exterior1st == 'ImStucc' | Exterior2nd == 'ImStucc', 1, 0),
  ExtMet = ifelse(Exterior1st == 'MetalSd' | Exterior2nd == 'MetalSd', 1, 0),
  ExtPly = ifelse(Exterior1st == 'Plywood' | Exterior2nd == 'Plywood', 1, 0),
  ExtStc = ifelse(Exterior1st == 'Stucco' | Exterior2nd == 'Stucco', 1, 0),
  ExtVin = ifelse(Exterior1st == 'VinylSd' | Exterior2nd == 'VinylSd', 1, 0),
  ExtWSd = ifelse(Exterior1st == 'Wd Sdng' | Exterior2nd == 'Wd Sdng', 1, 0),
  ExtWSh = case_when(
    Exterior1st %in% c('WdShing', 'Wd Shng') ~ 1,
    Exterior2nd %in% c('WdShing', 'Wd Shng') ~ 1,
    TRUE ~ 0
  ),
  ExtOth = case_when(
    Exterior1st %in% c('AsphShn', 'CBlock', 'Stone', 'Other') ~ 1,
    Exterior2nd %in% c('AsphShn', 'CBlock', 'Stone', 'Other') ~ 1,
    TRUE ~ 0
  )
)

ext_vars <- c('ExtAsb', 'ExtBrk', 'ExtCem', 'ExtHdB', 'ExtImS', 'ExtMet', 'ExtPly', 'ExtStc', 'ExtVin', 'ExtWSd', 'ExtWSh', 'ExtOth')
head(subset(train_form[c('Exterior1st', 'Exterior2nd', ext_vars)], as.character(Exterior1st) != as.character(Exterior2nd)))
```

```{r}
# Remove Exterior1st & 2nd

train_form$Exterior2nd <- NULL
```

# OLS Linear Regression

## Initial Linear Regression Model

### p Selection via Cross Validation

Proceed with 10-fold forward stepwise selection cross validation to determine optimal number of predictors.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}
set.seed(5130)
rec <- recipe(SalePrice ~ ., data = train_form) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) 

ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = 'repeatedcv',
  number = 10,
  repeats = 5,
  returnResamp = 'all'
)

grid <- expand.grid(nvmax = 1:175)

linreg_form <- train(
  rec,
  data = train_form,
  method = 'leapForward',
  trControl = ctrl,
  tuneGrid = grid,
  metric = 'RMSE'
)
```

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=3}
df <- linreg_form$resample %>%
  dplyr::mutate(rep = str_split_i(Resample, '\\.', 2)) %>%
  group_by(rep, nvmax) %>%
  summarise(mean_RMSE = mean(RMSE))

ggplot(df, aes(x = nvmax, y = mean_RMSE)) + 
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(.~rep) +
  labs(x = 'Predictors', y = 'RMSE', title = 'LinReg (Formatted Data) CV RMSE by Predictor Count')
```

Local minima appear fairly consistently around p = 50, p = 75, p = 100, and p = 150

### Cross Validation RMSE

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
set.seed(2283)

best_p <- linreg_form$bestTune[[1]]
rec <- recipe(SalePrice ~ ., data = train_form) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) 

ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = 'repeatedcv',
  number = 10,
  repeats = 10,
  returnResamp = 'all'
)

grid <- expand.grid(nvmax = c(50, 75, 100, 150, best_p))

linreg_rmse_form <- train(
  rec,
  data = train_form,
  method = 'leapForward',
  trControl = ctrl,
  tuneGrid = grid,
  metric = 'RMSE'
)
```

```{r}
df <- linreg_rmse_form$resample %>%
  dplyr::mutate(rep = str_split_i(Resample, '\\.', 2)) %>%
  group_by(rep, nvmax) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(mean_rmse = mean(RMSE))

write.csv(df, file = 'Data/linreg_form_cv_rmse.csv')

ggplot(df, aes(x = factor(nvmax), y = mean_rmse)) +
  geom_boxplot() + 
  labs(
    x = 'Number of Predictors', 
    y = 'RMSE',
    title = 'Distributions of LinReg (Formatted Data) CV RMSE by Predictor Count'
  )

linreg_rmse_form_stats <- df %>%
  group_by(nvmax) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_RMSE = mean(mean_rmse),
    med_RMSE = median(mean_rmse),
    sd_RMSE = sd(mean_rmse),
    IQR_RMSE = IQR(mean_rmse)
    )
linreg_rmse_form_stats
```

Caret determined p = 167 as the optimal number of predictors. This appears to be the case.

### Model Diagnostics

```{r}
prep <- prep(rec, training = train_form)
lm_df <- bake(prep, new_data = NULL)
preds <- names(coef(linreg_rmse_form$finalModel, id = 167))[-1]
eq <- reformulate(
  termlabels = preds,
  response = 'SalePrice'
)

lm_form <- lm(eq, data = lm_df)

plot(lm_form)
```

From residuals vs fitted and scale-location plots heteroscedasticity does not seem to be a major problem. There is a slight bend but no strange patterns emerge. Per the QQ plot the vast majority of residuals conform to a normal distribution. Point 1291 is a high-leverage point with a > 1 Cook's distance.

### Response Variable Analysis

Let's see if log-transforming SalePrice might improve predictive accuracy

```{r, fig.width=15, fig.height=15}
num_vars <- names(train)[!(names(train) %in% cat_vars)]
num_preds <- num_vars
num_preds <- num_preds[num_preds != 'Id']
num_preds <- num_preds[num_preds != 'SalePrice']

train_pivot <- train_form %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(num_preds),
               names_to = 'Predictor',
               values_to = 'Value')
ggplot(train_pivot, aes(x = Value, y = SalePrice)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(. ~ factor(Predictor, levels = num_preds), scales = 'free_x') +
  labs(title = 'SalePrice vs All Quantitative Predictors')

train_quant <- train_form[num_preds]
train_quant_trans <- train_quant
train_quant_trans$SalePrice <- log(train_form$SalePrice)
train_pivot <- train_quant_trans %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(num_preds),
               names_to = 'Predictor',
               values_to = 'Value')
ggplot(train_pivot, aes(x = Value, y = SalePrice)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(. ~ factor(Predictor, levels = num_preds), scales = 'free_x') +
  labs(title = 'log(SalePrice) vs All Quantitative Predictors')

sapply(num_preds, function(x) {
  corr <- cor(train_quant[x], train_form$SalePrice)
  log_corr <- cor(train_quant[x], log(train_form$SalePrice))
  return(c(corr, log_corr))
})
```

19 out of 33 predictors saw some increase in correlation following the log-transformation of the response. The scatterplots with the log-transformed resposnse also appear slightly more linear, with less "fanning out" as the predictor increases.

### Quantitative Predictor Analysis

Let's see if log transforming the predictors makes their relationships with log(SalePrice) more linear.

```{r, fig.width=15, fig.height=15}
train_pivot <- train_form %>%
  dplyr::mutate(SalePrice = log(SalePrice)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(c(num_preds)),
               names_to = 'Predictor',
               values_to = 'Value')
ggplot(train_pivot, aes(x = Value, y = SalePrice)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(. ~ factor(Predictor, levels = num_preds), scales = 'free_x') +
  labs(title = 'log(SalePrice) vs All Quantitative Predictors')

train_quant <- train_form[num_preds]
train_quant_trans <- dplyr::mutate(train_quant, across(everything(), log1p))
train_quant_trans$SalePrice <- log(train_form$SalePrice)
train_pivot <- train_quant_trans %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(num_preds),
               names_to = 'Predictor',
               values_to = 'Value')
ggplot(train_pivot, aes(x = Value, y = SalePrice)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(. ~ factor(Predictor, levels = num_preds), scales = 'free_x') +
  labs(title = 'log(SalePrice) vs Log of All Quantitative Predictors')

sapply(num_preds, function(x) {
  corr <- cor(train_quant[x], log(train_form$SalePrice))
  log_corr <- cor(train_quant_trans[x], log(train_form$SalePrice))
  return(c(corr, log_corr))
})
```

LotArea, OpenPorchSF, and EnclosedPorch both saw a noticeable increase in correlation. Visually, the relationships between these predictors and log(SalePrice) appear slightly more linear. Outliers are less pronounced.

WoodDeckSF also appears to have a more linear relationship with log(SalePrice) following a log transformation, with less fanning out.

## Linear Regression Model on Refined Data

This model uses a refined version of the training data. Conforming it better to the assumptions of linear regression by removing a high-leverage point and log-transforming LotArea, OpenPorchSF, and EnclosedPorch, which noticeably increased their correlation with log(SalePrice), and WoodDeckSF, whose relationship with log(SalePrice) appeared more linear. SalePrice is also log-transformed.

```{r}
train_ref <- train_form
train_ref$SalePrice <- log(train_ref$SalePrice)
train_ref$LotArea <- log1p(train_ref$LotArea)
train_ref$OpenPorchSF <- log1p(train_ref$OpenPorchSF)
train_ref$EnclosedPorch <- log1p(train_ref$EnclosedPorch)
train_ref$WoodDeckSF <- log1p(train_ref$WoodDeckSF)
train_ref$X1stFlrSF <- NULL
train_ref$GarageArea <- NULL
train_ref$TotRmsAbvGrd <- NULL
train_ref <- train_ref[-1291, ]
```

### p selection via Cross Validation

```{r}
# log RMSE to raw converter function
f_raw_RMSE <- function(data, lev = NULL, model = NULL) {
  raw_obs <- exp(data$obs)
  raw_pred <- exp(data$pred)
  
  raw_rmse <- sqrt(mean((raw_obs - raw_pred)^2))
  
  return(c(raw_RMSE = raw_rmse))
}
```

```{r, warning=FALSE}
set.seed(2556)
rec <- recipe(SalePrice ~ ., data = train_ref) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) 

ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = 'repeatedcv',
  number = 10,
  repeats = 5,
  returnResamp = 'all',
  summaryFunction = f_raw_RMSE
)

grid <- expand.grid(nvmax = 1:175)

linreg_ref <- train(
  rec,
  data = train_ref,
  method = 'leapForward',
  trControl = ctrl,
  tuneGrid = grid,
  metric = 'raw_RMSE'
)
```

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=3}
df <- linreg_ref$resample %>%
  dplyr::mutate(rep = str_split_i(Resample, '\\.', 2)) %>%
  group_by(rep, nvmax) %>%
  summarise(mean_RMSE = mean(raw_RMSE))

ggplot(df, aes(x = nvmax, y = mean_RMSE)) + 
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(.~rep) +
  labs(x = 'Predictors', y = 'RMSE', title = 'LinReg (Refined Data) CV RMSE by Predictor Count')

linreg_ref$bestTune
```

Caret determined p = 1 to be the best. Around p = 75, p = 100, and p = 150 seem like local minimums, and reasonable values for the optimal number of predictors.

# Shrinkage

## Ridge Regression

### Formatted Data

We proceed with fitting a ridge regression model on the formatted data.

#### Lambda Selection via Cross Validation

```{r}
set.seed(8615)

rec <- recipe(SalePrice ~ ., data = train_form) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) 

ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = 'repeatedcv',
  number = 10,
  repeats = 5,
  returnResamp = 'all'
)

grid <- expand.grid(alpha = 0, lambda = 10^seq(1, 5, length = 100))

ridge_form <- train(
  rec,
  data = train_form,
  method = 'glmnet',
  trControl = ctrl,
  tuneGrid = grid,
  metric = 'RMSE'
)
```

```{r, fig.width=12, fig.height=3}
df <- ridge_form$resample %>%
  dplyr::mutate(rep = str_split_i(Resample, '\\.', 2)) %>%
  group_by(rep, lambda) %>%
  summarise(mean_RMSE = mean(RMSE))

ggplot(df, aes(x = lambda, y = mean_RMSE)) + 
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(.~rep) +
  labs(x = 'Lambda', y = 'RMSE', title = 'Ridge Regression (Formatted Data) CV RMSE by Lambda')
```

```{r, fig.width=12, fig.height=3}
ggplot(df, aes(x = lambda, y = mean_RMSE)) +

  facet_grid(.~rep) +
  labs(x = 'Lambda', y = 'RMSE', title = 'Ridge Regression (Formatted Data) CV RMSE by Lambda') +

ridge_form$bestTune
```

## Elastic Net

### Formatted Data

#### Alpha and Lambda Selection via Cross Validation

```{r}
set.seed(2371)
rec <- recipe(SalePrice ~ ., data = train_form) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) 

ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = 'repeatedcv',
  number = 10,
  repeats = 3,
  returnResamp = 'all'
)

grid <- expand.grid(alpha = seq(0, 1, by = .1), lambda = 10^seq(1, 4, length = 100))

elastic_form <- train(
  rec,
  data = train_form,
  method = 'glmnet',
  trControl = ctrl,
  tuneGrid = grid,
  metric = 'RMSE'
)
```

```{r, fig.width=12, fig.height=20}
df <- elastic_form$resample %>%
  dplyr::mutate(rep = str_split_i(Resample, '\\.', 2)) %>%
  group_by(rep, alpha, lambda) %>%
  summarise(mean_RMSE = mean(RMSE)) 
df$alpha <- factor(df$alpha)

ggplot(df, aes(x = lambda, y = mean_RMSE, color = alpha)) + 
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(.~rep) +
  labs(x = 'Lambda', y = 'RMSE', title = 'Elastic (Formatted Data) CV RMSE by Alpha and Lambda')
```

```{r}
elastic_form$bestTune
```

We seem to see 2 areas where CV RMSE is the lowest. (Alpha \~ .1, Lambda \~ 4500), and (Alpha \~ .9, Lambda \~ 1000) Let's analyze those regions closer.

```{r}
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) %>%

  repeats = 5,

knn_form <- caret::train(

  data = train_form,
  method = 'knn',

  tuneGrid = grid,

)
```

# General Additive Models

Due to computational limits only the variables selected via CV on the linear regression models will be considered.

## Smoothing Splines

### Formatted Data

```{r}
# Get formatted data
rec <- recipe(SalePrice ~ ., data = train_form) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) 
prep_form <- prep(rec, training = train_form)
linreg_rmse_form_df <- bake(prep_form, new_data = NULL)

preds_form <- names(lm_form$coefficients)[-1]
df_form <- linreg_rmse_form_df[c(preds_form, 'SalePrice')]
```

```{r}
# Determine which preds to smooth in formatted data
num_vars_form <- names(
  df_form[
    sapply(df_form, function(x) {
      ifelse(is.numeric(x) == TRUE & setequal(unique(x), c(0, 1)) == FALSE, TRUE, FALSE)
    })
  ]
)
num_vars_form <- num_vars_form[num_vars_form != 'SalePrice']

sapply(df_form[num_vars_form], function(x) {
  length(unique(x))
})
```

Smoothing functions allow for a model to account for a predictor whose relationship with the response changes as it changes. Any predictor with a low amount of unique levels shouldn't be smoothed. OverallQual, OverallCond, LowQualFinSF, BsmtFullBath, BsmtHalfBath, FullBath, HalfBath, BedroomAbvGr, KitchenAbvGr, TotRmsAbvGrd, Fireplaces, GarageCars, X3SsnPorch, PoolArea, MiscVal, and YrSold probably do not have too complicated relationships with SalePrice due to lack of complexity.

```{r}
smooth_vars_form <- num_vars_form[!(num_vars_form %in% c('OverallQual', 'OverallCond', 'LowQualFinSF', 'BsmtFullBath', 'BsmtHalfBath', 'FullBath', 'HalfBath', 'BedroomAbvGr', 'KitchenAbvGr', 'TotRmsAbvGrd', 'Fireplaces', 'GarageCars', 'X3SsnPorch', 'PoolArea', 'MiscVal', 'YrSold'))]
other_vars_form <- names(df_form)[!(names(df_form) %in% smooth_vars_form)] 
other_vars_form <- other_vars_form[other_vars_form != 'SalePrice']

smooth_terms_form <- paste(paste0('s(', smooth_vars_form, ')'), collapse = ' + ')
other_terms_form <- paste(other_vars_form, collapse = '+')
formula_form <- as.formula(paste('SalePrice ~', smooth_terms_form, '+', other_terms_form))
```

#### Cross Validation RMSE

5-fold CV due to computational limits

```{r}
set.seed(8631)

smth_spline_rmse_form <- rep(0, 5)
folds <- createFolds(df_form$SalePrice, k = 5)
for (i in 1:5) {
  test_fold <- df_form[folds[[i]],]
  train_folds <- df_form[-folds[[i]],]
  
  fit <- bam(formula_form, data = train_folds, method = 'REML', select = TRUE)
  preds <- predict(fit, newdata = test_fold)
  
  smth_spline_rmse_form[i] <- sqrt(mean((test_fold$SalePrice - preds)^2))
}
```

```{r}
df <- data.frame(
  rep = c('Rep01', 'Rep02', 'Rep03', 'Rep04', 'Rep05'),
  mean_RMSE = smth_spline_rmse_form 
)
write.csv(df, file = 'Data/smth_form_cv_rmse.csv')

smth_spline_rmse_form_stats <- data.frame(
  mean_RMSE = mean(smth_spline_rmse_form),
  med_RMSE = median(smth_spline_rmse_form),
  sd_RMSE = sd(smth_spline_rmse_form),
  IQR_RMSE = IQR(smth_spline_rmse_form)
)
smth_spline_rmse_form_stats
```

### Refined Data

```{r}
# Get refined data
rec <- recipe(SalePrice ~ ., data = train_ref) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) 
prep_ref <- prep(rec, training = train_ref)
linreg_rmse_ref_df <- bake(prep_ref, new_data = NULL)

preds_ref <- names(final_lm_ref$coefficients[-1])
df_ref <- linreg_rmse_ref_df[c(preds_ref, 'SalePrice')]
```

```{r}
# Determine which preds to smooth in formatted data
num_vars_ref <- names(
  df_ref[
    sapply(df_ref, function(x) {
      ifelse(is.numeric(x) == TRUE & setequal(unique(x), c(0, 1)) == FALSE, TRUE, FALSE)
    })
  ]
)
num_vars_ref <- num_vars_ref[num_vars_ref != 'SalePrice']

sapply(df_ref[num_vars_ref], function(x) {
  length(unique(x))
})
```

As with the formatted data, only the variables with large amount of levels will be smoothed. OverallQual, OverallCond, BsmtFullBath, BsmtHalfBath, FullBath, HalfBath, BedroomAbvGr, KitchenAbvGr, Fireplaces, GarageCars, X3SsnPorch, PoolArea, and MiscVal probably don't have too complex a relationship with SalePrice and aren't worth smoothing.

```{r}
smooth_vars_ref <- num_vars_ref[!(num_vars_ref %in% c('OverallQual', 'OverallCond', 'BsmtFullBath', 'BsmtHalfBath', 'FullBath', 'HalfBath', 'BedroomAbvGr', 'KitchenAbvGr', 'Fireplaces', 'GarageCars', 'X3SsnPorch', 'PoolArea', 'MiscVal'))]
other_vars_ref <- names(df_ref)[!(names(df_ref) %in% smooth_vars_ref)] 
other_vars_ref <- other_vars_ref[other_vars_ref != 'SalePrice']

smooth_terms_ref <- paste(paste0('s(', smooth_vars_ref, ')'), collapse = ' + ')
other_terms_ref <- paste(other_vars_ref, collapse = '+')
formula_ref <- as.formula(paste('SalePrice ~', smooth_terms_ref, '+', other_terms_ref))
```

#### Cross Validation RMSE

5-fold CV due to computational limitations.

```{r}
set.seed(2778)

smth_spline_rmse_ref <- rep(0, 5)
folds <- createFolds(df_ref$SalePrice, k = 5)
for (i in 1:5) {
  test_fold <- df_ref[folds[[i]],]
  train_folds <- df_ref[-folds[[i]],]
  
  fit <- bam(formula_ref, data = train_folds, method = 'REML', select = TRUE)
  preds <- predict(fit, newdata = test_fold)
  
  smth_spline_rmse_ref[i] <- sqrt(mean((exp(test_fold$SalePrice) - exp(preds))^2))
}
```


# Decision Trees

## Regression Tree

### Formatted Data

#### Size Selection via Cross Validation

```{r}
set.seed(8276)
rec <- recipe(SalePrice ~ ., data = train_form) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) 

ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = 'repeatedcv',
  number = 10,
  repeats = 5,
  returnResamp = 'all'
)

grid <- expand.grid(cp = 10^seq(-3, 1, length = 100))

regtree_form <- train(
  rec,
  data = train_form,
  method = 'rpart',
  trControl = ctrl,
  tuneGrid = grid,
  metric = 'RMSE'
)
```

```{r, fig.width=12, fig.height=3}
df <- regtree_form$resample %>%
  dplyr::mutate(rep = str_split_i(Resample, '\\.', 2)) %>%
  group_by(rep, cp) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(mean_RMSE = mean(RMSE))

ggplot(df, aes(x = cp, y = mean_RMSE)) + 
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(.~rep) +
  labs(x = 'Complexity Parameter', y = 'RMSE', title = 'Reg Tree (Formatted Data) by CP')
```

## Boosting

### Formatted Data

#### Parameter Selection via Cross Validation

We proceed with only 1 iteration of CV due to computational limitations to determine optimal ranges for maximum depth (max_depth), proportion of observations per tree (subsample), proportion of predictors per tree (colsample_bytree), and minimum size for a node split (min_weight).

```{r}
set.seed(7330)
mod_mat <- model.matrix(SalePrice ~ . - 1, data = train_form)
dmat_form <- xgb.DMatrix(
  data = mod_mat,
  label = train_form$SalePrice
)

form_max_depths <- c()
form_subsamples <- c()
form_colsamples <- c()
form_min_weights <- c()
form_rmses <- c()
for (max_depth in c(3,4,5)) {
  for (subsample in c(.25, .5, .75, 1)) {
    for (colsample in c(.25, .5, .75, 1)) {
      for (min_weight in c(5, 10, 20)) {
        set.seed(7330)
        params <- list(
          objective = 'reg:squarederror',
          eval_metric = 'rmse',
          eta = .1,
          max_depth = max_depth,
          min_child_weight = min_weight,
          gamma = 0,
          subsample = subsample,
          colsample_bytree = colsample,
          seed = 7330
        )
        boost_cv <- xgb.cv(
          params = params,
          data = dmat_form,
          nrounds = 2000,
          nfold = 10,
          early_stopping_rounds = 50,
          verbose = FALSE
        )
        form_max_depths <- c(form_max_depths, max_depth)
        form_subsamples <- c(form_subsamples, subsample)
        form_colsamples <- c(form_colsamples, colsample)
        form_min_weights <- c(form_min_weights, min_weight)
        form_rmses <- c(form_rmses, boost_cv$early_stop$best_score)
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```{r}
boost_form_stats <- data.frame(
  rmse = form_rmses,
  max_depth = form_max_depths,
  subsample = form_subsamples,
  colsample_bytree = form_colsamples,
  min_child_weight = form_min_weights
)
boost_form_stats[order(boost_form_stats$rmse), ]
```

To narrow down ideal parameter values, we look at which parameter values are most common among the boosted models with the best RMSE values. This was determined by limiting the values to only those within 1 standard deviation or 1 IQR of the minimum.

```{r}
boost_form_win_1sd <- subset(boost_form_stats, rmse <= min(boost_form_stats$rmse) + sd(boost_form_stats$rmse))
boost_form_win_1iqr <- subset(boost_form_stats, rmse <= min(boost_form_stats$rmse) + IQR(boost_form_stats$rmse))
```

```{r}
i_vec <- c(2,3,4,5)
rm_i <- 1
for (i1 in 2:5) {
  i_vec <- i_vec[-rm_i]
  for (i2 in i_vec) {
    tab_name_sd <- paste('Models w/in 1 SD of Min.,', names(boost_form_stats)[i1], 'vs', names(boost_form_stats)[i2])
    tab_name_iqr <- paste('Models w/in 1 IQR of Min.,', names(boost_form_stats)[i1], 'vs', names(boost_form_stats)[i2])
    
    tab_sd <- as.data.frame.matrix(
      addmargins(table(boost_form_win_1sd[, i1], boost_form_win_1sd[, i2]))
    )
    tab_sd <- gt(tab_sd, rownames_to_stub = TRUE) %>%
      tab_header(title = tab_name_sd) %>%
      tab_stubhead(label = names(boost_form_stats)[i1]) %>%
      tab_spanner(
        label = names(boost_form_stats)[i2],
        columns = everything()
      )
    
    tab_iqr <- as.data.frame.matrix(
      addmargins(table(boost_form_win_1iqr[, i1], boost_form_win_1iqr[, i2]))
    )
    tab_iqr <- gt(tab_iqr, rownames_to_stub = TRUE) %>%
      tab_header(title = tab_name_iqr) %>%
      tab_stubhead(label = names(boost_form_stats)[i1]) %>%
      tab_spanner(
        label = names(boost_form_stats)[i2],
        columns = everything()
      )
    print(tab_sd)
    print(tab_iqr)
  }
}
```

The most dominant parameter (most common among the models with RMSE within 1 sd of the minimum) was either max_depth = 5 min_child_weight = 20, both at 10/19

When looking at the most dominant parameter given the previous parameter was either max_depth = 5 or min_child_weight = 20. With max_depth = 5 it was min_child_weight = 20, at 5/10 for models within 1 sd of the minimum and 9/16 for models within 1 IQR of the minimum. For min_child_weight = 20, it was subsample = 0.5 with 6/10 for models within 1 sd of the minimum and 11/19 for models within 1 IQR of the minimum. Proceed with min_child_weight = 20 and subsample = 0.5.

For subsample = 0.5, max_depth = 5 was the most dominant for models within 1 sd of the minimum, though it evened out when taking into account models within 1 IQR of the minimum. For min_child_weight = 20, max_depth = 4 and max_depth = 5 were very similar, though 5 edged 4 out slightly. Proceed with max_depth = 5.

At max_depth = 5, colsample_bytree = 0.25 and colsample_bytree = 0.5 were about equivalent for models within 1 sd of the minimum, though solsample_bytree = 0.5 pulled ahead slightly when models within 1 IQR of the minimum were added. FOr subsample = 0.5, 0.75 slightly edged 0.25 out for models within 1 sd of the minimum, though including models within 1 IQR of the minimum all parameter values were about equal. For min_child_weight = 20, 0.25, 0.5, and 0.75 were about equivalent with 0.75 being the most dominant for models within 1 sd of the minimum, and it and 0.5 pulled slightly ahead once models within 1 IQR of the minimum were also taking into account. Proceed with colsample_bytree = 0.5.

### Refined Data

#### Parameter Selection via Cross Validation

```{r}
# Custom metric to convert log(SalePrice) to Saleprice for xgboost
f_boost_raw_RMSE <- function(preds, dtrain) {
  actual_log <- getinfo(dtrain, 'label')

  actual_raw <- exp(actual_log)
  preds_raw  <- exp(preds)

  rmse <- sqrt(mean((actual_raw - preds_raw)^2))

  return(list(
    metric = 'raw_rmse',
    value = rmse
  ))
}
```

A single CV iteration was conducted to determine reasonable parameter values.

```{r}
mod_mat <- model.matrix(SalePrice ~ . - 1, data = train_ref)
dmat_ref <- xgb.DMatrix(
  data = mod_mat,
  label = train_ref$SalePrice
)

ref_max_depths <- c()
ref_subsamples <- c()
ref_colsamples <- c()
ref_min_weights <- c()
ref_rmses <- c()
for (max_depth in c(3,4,5)) {
  for (subsample in c(.25, .5, .75, 1)) {
    for (colsample in c(.25, .5, .75, 1)) {
      for (min_weight in c(5, 10, 20)) {
        set.seed(7116)
        params <- list(
          objective = "reg:squarederror",
          eta = .1,
          max_depth = max_depth,
          min_child_weight = min_weight,
          gamma = 0,
          subsample = subsample,
          colsample_bytree = colsample,
          seed = 7116
        )
        boost_cv <- xgb.cv(
          params = params,
          data = dmat_ref,
          nrounds = 2000,
          nfold = 10,
          custom_metric = f_boost_raw_RMSE,
          maximize = FALSE,
          early_stopping_rounds = 50,
          verbose = FALSE
        )
        ref_max_depths <- c(ref_max_depths, max_depth)
        ref_subsamples <- c(ref_subsamples, subsample)
        ref_colsamples <- c(ref_colsamples, colsample)
        ref_min_weights <- c(ref_min_weights, min_weight)
        ref_rmses <- c(ref_rmses, boost_cv$early_stop$best_score)
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```{r}
boost_ref_stats <- data.frame(
  rmse = ref_rmses,
  max_depth = ref_max_depths,
  subsample = ref_subsamples,
  colsample_bytree = ref_colsamples,
  min_child_weight = ref_min_weights
)
boost_ref_stats[order(boost_ref_stats$rmse), ]
```

```{r}
boost_ref_win_1sd <- subset(boost_ref_stats, rmse <= min(boost_ref_stats$rmse) + sd(boost_ref_stats$rmse))
boost_ref_win_1iqr <- subset(boost_ref_stats, rmse <= min(boost_ref_stats$rmse) + IQR(boost_ref_stats$rmse))
```

```{r}
i_vec <- c(2,3,4,5)
rm_i <- 1
for (i1 in 2:5) {
  i_vec <- i_vec[-rm_i]
  for (i2 in i_vec) {
    tab_name_sd <- paste('Models w/in 1 SD of Min.,', names(boost_ref_stats)[i1], 'vs', names(boost_ref_stats)[i2])
    tab_name_iqr <- paste('Models w/in 1 IQR of Min.,', names(boost_ref_stats)[i1], 'vs', names(boost_ref_stats)[i2])
    
    tab_sd <- as.data.frame.matrix(
      addmargins(table(boost_ref_win_1sd[, i1], boost_ref_win_1sd[, i2]))
    )
    tab_sd <- gt(tab_sd, rownames_to_stub = TRUE) %>%
      tab_header(title = tab_name_sd) %>%
      tab_stubhead(label = names(boost_ref_stats)[i1]) %>%
      tab_spanner(
        label = names(boost_ref_stats)[i2],
        columns = everything()
      )
    
    tab_iqr <- as.data.frame.matrix(
      addmargins(table(boost_ref_win_1iqr[, i1], boost_ref_win_1iqr[, i2]))
    )
    tab_iqr <- gt(tab_iqr, rownames_to_stub = TRUE) %>%
      tab_header(title = tab_name_iqr) %>%
      tab_stubhead(label = names(boost_ref_stats)[i1]) %>%
      tab_spanner(
        label = names(boost_ref_stats)[i2],
        columns = everything()
      )
    print(tab_sd)
    print(tab_iqr)
  }
}
```

Max_depth = 3, subsample = 0.5, and min_child_weight = 20 were similarly dominant for models within 1 sd of the minimum, at 8/11, 9/11, and 8/11 respectively. For models within 1 IQR of the minimum, max_depth = 3 had 17/30, subsample = 0.5 had 16/30, and min_child_weight had 17/30. 

For models with max_depth = 3, 6/8 within 1 sd and 9/17 within 1 IQR of the minimum models had subsample = 0.5. 5/8 within 1 sd and 9/16 within 1 IQR of the minimum models had min_child_weight = 20. 

For models with subsample = 0.5, 6/9 within 1 sd and 8/16 within 1 IQR of the minimum models had min_child_weight = 20.

Thus the combination of max_depth = 3, subsample = 0.5, and min_child_Weight = 20 seems quite dominant. Proceed with those values.

For max_depth = 3, colsample_bytree = 0.25 at 4/8 within 1 sd and 8/17 within 1 IQR of the minimum was the most dominant. For subsample = 0.5, colsample_bytree = 0.25 was dominant at  with 5/9 within 1 sd and 8/16 within 1 IQR of the minimum. For min_child_weight = 20, colsample_bytree also performed quite well, with 4/8 within 1 sd and 7/14 within 1 IQR of the minimum. Proceed with colsample_bytree = 0.25

#### Data Formatting

```{r}

  # MSSubClass

  dplyr::mutate(
    MSSubClass = case_when(
      MSSubClass == '40' ~ '20',
      MSSubClass == '150' ~ '120',

    ),

  # Condition1 & Condition2

    ),

    ),
    CondPos = case_when(
      Condition1 %in% c('PosN', 'PosA') | Condition2 %in% c('PosN', 'PosA') ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    CondRRn = case_when(
      Condition1 %in% c('RRNn', 'RRAn') | Condition2 %in% c('RRNn', 'RRAn') ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    CondRRe = case_when(
      Condition1 %in% c('RRNe', 'RRAe') | Condition2 %in% c('RRNe', 'RRAe') ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ 0
    )
  )
test_form$Condition1 <- NULL
test_form$Condition2 <- NULL

test_form <- test_form %>%
  # HouseStyle
  dplyr::mutate(
    HouseStyle = case_when(
      HouseStyle %in% c('2.5Fin', '2.5Unf') ~ '2.5Story',
      TRUE ~ as.character(HouseStyle)
    ),
    HouseStyle = factor(HouseStyle)
  ) %>%
  # RoofStyle
  dplyr::mutate(
    RoofStyle = case_when(
      RoofStyle %in% c('Flat', 'Gambrel', 'Mansard', 'Shed') ~ 'Other',
      TRUE ~ as.character(RoofStyle)
    ),
    RoofStyle = factor(RoofStyle, levels = c('Gable', 'Hip', 'Flat', 'Other'))
  ) %>%
  # RoofMatl
  dplyr::mutate(
    RoofMatl = case_when(
      RoofMatl %in% c('ClyTile', 'Membran', 'Metal', 'Roll', 'WdShake', 'WdShngl') ~ 'Other',
      RoofMatl == 'Tar&Grv' ~ 'TarGrv',
      TRUE ~ as.character(RoofMatl)
    ),
    RoofMatl = factor(RoofMatl)
  ) %>%
  # Exterior1st & Exterior2nd
  dplyr::mutate(
    ExtAsb = ifelse(Exterior1st == 'AsbShng' | Exterior2nd == 'AsbShng', 1, 0),
    ExtBrk = case_when(
      Exterior1st %in% c('BrkComm', 'Brk Cmn', 'BrkFace') ~ 1,
      Exterior2nd %in% c('BrkComm', 'Brk Cmn', 'BrkFace') ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    ExtCem = case_when(
      Exterior1st %in% c('CemntBd', 'CmentBd') ~ 1,
      Exterior2nd %in% c('CemntBd', 'CmentBd') ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    ExtHdB = ifelse(Exterior1st == 'HdBoard' | Exterior2nd == 'HdBoard', 1, 0),
    ExtImS = ifelse(Exterior1st == 'ImStucc' | Exterior2nd == 'ImStucc', 1, 0),
    ExtMet = ifelse(Exterior1st == 'MetalSd' | Exterior2nd == 'MetalSd', 1, 0),
    ExtPly = ifelse(Exterior1st == 'Plywood' | Exterior2nd == 'Plywood', 1, 0),
    ExtStc = ifelse(Exterior1st == 'Stucco' | Exterior2nd == 'Stucco', 1, 0),
    ExtVin = ifelse(Exterior1st == 'VinylSd' | Exterior2nd == 'VinylSd', 1, 0),
    ExtWSd = ifelse(Exterior1st == 'Wd Sdng' | Exterior2nd == 'Wd Sdng', 1, 0),
    ExtWSh = case_when(
      Exterior1st %in% c('WdShing', 'Wd Shng') ~ 1,
      Exterior2nd %in% c('WdShing', 'Wd Shng') ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    ExtOth = case_when(
      Exterior1st %in% c('AsphShn', 'CBlock', 'Stone', 'Other') ~ 1,
      Exterior2nd %in% c('AsphShn', 'CBlock', 'Stone', 'Other') ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ 0
    )
  )
test_form$Exterior1st <- NULL
test_form$Exterior2nd <- NULL

test_form <- test_form %>%
  # ExterCond
  dplyr::mutate(
    ExterCond = case_when(
      ExterCond == 'Ex' ~ 'Gd',
      ExterCond == 'Po' ~ 'Fa',
      TRUE ~ as.character(ExterCond)
    ),
    ExterCond = factor(ExterCond)
  ) %>%
  # Foundation
  dplyr::mutate(
    Foundation = ifelse(Foundation %in% c('Slab', 'Stone', 'Wood'), 'Other', as.character(Foundation)),
    Foundation = factor(Foundation)
  ) %>%
  # BsmtCond
  dplyr::mutate(
    BsmtCond = ifelse(BsmtCond == 'Po', 'Fa', as.character(BsmtCond)),
    BsmtCond = factor(BsmtCond)
  ) %>%
  # BsmtFinType1 & BsmtFinType2
  dplyr::mutate(
    BsmtALQ = ifelse(BsmtFinType1 == 'ALQ' | BsmtFinType2 == 'ALQ', 1, 0),
    BsmtBLQ = ifelse(BsmtFinType1 == 'BLQ' | BsmtFinType2 == 'BLQ', 1, 0),
    BsmtGLQ = ifelse(BsmtFinType1 == 'GLQ' | BsmtFinType2 == 'GLQ', 1, 0),
    BsmtLwQ = ifelse(BsmtFinType1 == 'LwQ' | BsmtFinType2 == 'LwQ', 1, 0),
    BsmtRec = ifelse(BsmtFinType1 == 'Rec' | BsmtFinType2 == 'Rec', 1, 0),
    BsmtUnf = ifelse(BsmtFinType1 == 'Unf' | BsmtFinType2 == 'Unf', 1, 0)
  )
test_form$BsmtFinType1 <- NULL
test_form$BsmtFinType2 <- NULL

test_form <- test_form %>%
  # Heating
  dplyr::mutate(
    Heating = ifelse(Heating %in% c('Floor', 'Grav', 'OthW', 'Wall'), 'Other', as.character(Heating)),
    Heating = factor(Heating)
  ) %>%
  # Heating QC
  dplyr::mutate(
    HeatingQC = ifelse(HeatingQC == 'Po', 'Fa', as.character(HeatingQC)),
    HeatingQC = factor(HeatingQC)
  ) %>%
  # Electrical
  dplyr::mutate(
    Electrical = ifelse(Electrical %in% c('FuseF', 'FuseP', 'Mix'), 'Other', as.character(Electrical)),
    Electrical = factor(Electrical)
  ) %>%
  # Functional
  dplyr::mutate(
    Functional = ifelse(Functional %in% c('Maj1', 'Maj2', 'Sev'), 'Maj', as.character(Functional)),
    Functional = factor(Functional)
  ) %>%
  # GarageType
  dplyr::mutate(
    GarageType = ifelse(GarageType %in% c('2Types', 'CarPort'), 'Other', as.character(GarageType)),
    GarageType = factor(GarageType)
  ) %>%
  # GarageQual
  dplyr::mutate(
    GarageQual = case_when(
      GarageQual == 'Ex' ~ 'Gd',
      GarageQual == 'Po' ~ 'Fa',
      TRUE ~ as.character(GarageQual)
    ),
    GarageQual = factor(GarageQual)
  ) %>%
  # GarageCond
  dplyr::mutate(
    GarageCond = case_when(
      GarageCond == 'Ex' ~ 'Gd',
      GarageCond == 'Po' ~ 'Fa',
      TRUE ~ as.character(GarageCond)
    ),
    GarageCond = factor(GarageCond)
  )

# PoolQC
test_form$PoolQC <- NULL

test_form <- test_form %>%
  # MiscFeature
  dplyr::mutate(
    HasMisc = case_when(
      MiscFeature == 'NoMisc' ~ 0,
      MiscFeature != 'NoMisc' ~ 1
    )
  ) 
test_form$MiscFeature <- NULL

test_form <- test_form %>%
  # SaleType
  dplyr::mutate(
    SaleType = case_when(
      SaleType %in% c('Con', 'ConLD', 'ConLI', 'ConLw') ~ 'Con',
      SaleType %in% c('WD', 'CWD', 'Oth')  ~ 'WD',
      TRUE ~ as.character(SaleType)
    ),
    SaleType = factor(SaleType)
  ) %>%
  # SaleCondition
  dplyr::mutate(
    SaleCondition = ifelse(SaleCondition == 'AdjLand', 'Normal', as.character(SaleCondition)),
    SaleCondition = factor(SaleCondition)
  )
```
